title: Desk Training Questions — Fault Findings under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions
content:
# Fault Findings — Desk Training Questions

Questions answered for client services agents on the fault detection rule of Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions.

## The rule

Automated fault detection runs only at the tiers that include it, with the tier's number of rules enabled against the site's data. A flagged condition is reported to the owner only where its priority reaches the tier's reporting threshold, and it is notified inside the tier's notification period counted in business days from the day the rules flagged it. A flagged fault is a finding, not a work order: it becomes work only when the owner asks for it, under the maintenance agreement where the unit is covered or as demand service where it is not. Faults below the threshold are held in the data and shown on the dashboard without notification. Where the tier includes no fault detection, the analytics do not watch for faults at all, and the desk says so rather than promising that nothing has been found. Whether detection runs, the rule count, the threshold and the notification period are the figures fixed for the tier.

## Questions

**Is a fault flagged at a priority below the tier's threshold notified to the owner?** No. It is held in the data and shown on the dashboard, without notification.

**From when is the notification period counted?** From the day the rules flagged the condition, in business days.

**Does a flagged fault open a work order?** No. It is a finding. It becomes work only when the owner asks; the work then falls under the maintenance agreement where the unit is covered, or is demand service where it is not.

**An owner on a tier with no fault detection asks whether any faults were found.** The answer is that the analytics do not watch for faults at that tier — not that nothing was found.

**How many reportable faults stand open on a subscription?** The count of faults flagged since the term started whose priority is at or above the tier's threshold.

## Priority against threshold (hypothetical, threshold at low)

| Flagged priority | Reaches the threshold |
|---|---|
| informational | no |
| low | yes |
| medium | yes |
| high | yes |
| critical | yes |
